learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master advanced noun concepts, including differentiating between countable and uncountable nouns, identifying compound nouns, and understanding noun cases.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 You’ve known about 'naming words' since you were little. But nouns aren't just simple labels anymore! Some nouns you can count on your fingers, others you can't. Some are made of two words squished together! Let's explore the advanced classifications of nouns.

lesson_modules.module_title: 🔢 Countable and Uncountable Nouns (गणनीय और अगणनीय संज्ञा)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Countable nouns are things we can count using numbers (they have plural forms). Uncountable nouns are substances, concepts, or liquids that we cannot count directly (they do not have plural forms). We use words like 'much', 'some', or 'a little' with them.
examples_or_templates: Uncountable: water, information, music, sugar (You don't say 'three waters' or 'musics')

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A compound noun is made up of two or more existing words joined together to create a completely new meaning. They can be written as one word, two separate words, or with a hyphen.
examples_or_templates: Separate words: ice cream, bus stop

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The 'Case' of a noun tells us what job it is doing in the sentence. If it is the subject, it's in the Nominative Case. If it is the object, it's in the Objective Case. If it shows ownership, it's in the Possessive Case.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which of the following is an Uncountable Noun?
❓ In the sentence 'The teacher corrected the essay', what case is the word 'essay' in?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Form the plural of the compound noun: 'brother-in-law'.
subjective_practice.hint: Which word is the most important part of the compound? Make that word plural!

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Identify the uncountable noun in this sentence and fix the grammatical error: 'She gave me many advices regarding my career.'
subjective_practice.hint: Advice is an uncountable concept. You cannot say 'advices' or use 'many' with it.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite this phrase using the Possessive Case: 'The car belonging to the principal.'

activity_or_assignment.title: 🕵️ The Kitchen Counter Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Go to your kitchen and look around. Make a list of 5 Countable nouns (like an apple, a spoon) and 5 Uncountable nouns (like rice, oil, flour). Share your list with a parent to see if you got them all correct!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Countable nouns can be numbered and made plural. Uncountable nouns cannot be counted directly.
⭐ Compound nouns are created by joining two or more words (e.g., bedroom, dry-cleaning).
⭐ Nouns have Cases based on their role: Nominative (Subject), Objective (Object), or Possessive (Ownership).
